technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the Receptor client as a Java library using the existing project HTTP and JSON facilities where possible, with typed request/response models and a small service API for Diego/Receptor operations.
Separate stream and job definition persistence from deployment by introducing repository interfaces and moving deployment-specific behavior into service-layer components.
Define a runtime SPI around lifecycle, deployment, status, and teardown operations, with the existing Cloud Foundry implementation adapted as the initial provider.
Use the existing Spring XD persistence conventions and a relational/JDBC-backed repository for durable stream metadata, including restart and recovery state.
Implement streaming-pipeline support through the existing XD module and deployment abstractions, adding Spark/Spark Streaming integration rather than modifying Spark itself.
Expose Sqoop import options as individually bindable job parameters, while retaining compatibility with existing argument-based configuration where practical.
Treat documentation changes as versioned project documentation and include concrete configuration examples for escaping, nested jobs, workflows, and parameterized imports.
Use unit tests for isolated components and focused integration tests for persistence, runtime selection, Receptor calls, and streaming pipeline deployment.
assumptions: The work is performed by one developer and estimates represent active workdays, excluding calendar waiting time and external review delays.
An existing Spring XD codebase, build system, test framework, module conventions, and deployment abstractions are available and can be extended.
The target Java and Spring versions are the versions already used by the target Spring XD branch; upgrading the whole product to Spring Framework 6 and Java 17 is out of scope.
Receptor API behavior and the referenced receptor-client project are sufficiently documented or available for implementation; no changes to Receptor or Diego are required.
The initial runtime SPI implementation only needs to preserve the existing deployment target behavior; additional complete Mesos and on-prem implementations are out of scope.
The persistent stream repository can use the project's existing database and migration mechanism; introducing a new database product or distributed consensus mechanism is out of scope.
Streaming-pipeline work covers XD configuration, lifecycle integration, compatibility updates, and representative Spark/Spark Streaming tests, not development of a new Spark execution engine.
Import-option parameterization covers the options exposed by the existing Sqoop module and includes validation and backward-compatible handling of the legacy --args form where feasible.
Documentation is written in the repository's existing documentation format and does not require a separate documentation website redesign or translation.
CI infrastructure and test environments for the existing deployment target, database, and representative Spark integration are available.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing XD architecture, identify affected modules and extension points, map the eight user stories to components, define interfaces and data flows, and produce an implementation plan.
Create the Java client library, request and response models, API operations needed by XD, serialization and error handling, configuration support, and unit tests for successful and failed API calls.

activities.activity_name: Refactor stream and job definition repositories
activities.activity_description: Separate definition storage and retrieval responsibilities from module deployment concerns, introduce or adjust repository interfaces, migrate existing callers, preserve behavior, and add regression tests.

activities.activity_name: Design and implement pluggable runtime SPI
activities.activity_description: Define runtime lifecycle, deployment, status, and teardown contracts; implement runtime selection and configuration; adapt the current deployment target as the initial provider; and test provider isolation and selection.

activities.activity_name: Implement persistent stream repository and recovery support
activities.activity_description: Add durable stream metadata and lifecycle state storage using the existing persistence mechanism, implement restart/reestablishment behavior, handle duplicate or stale state, add schema migration where needed, and test failure recovery.

activities.activity_name: Implement streaming pipeline support for Spark and Spark Streaming
activities.activity_description: Update XD stream pipeline definitions, module configuration, runtime integration, compatibility handling for the supported Spark APIs, lifecycle behavior, and representative end-to-end or integration tests.

Enumerate current import options, expose them as typed or validated job parameters, update binding and command construction, document precedence and compatibility with --args, and add unit and integration coverage.
Add clear documentation and examples explaining double escaping of the null representation and the difference between shell, configuration, and job-level quoting.

activities.activity_name: Document nested batch jobs and workflows
activities.activity_description: Create end-user reference documentation with syntax, configuration examples, execution semantics, limitations, and troubleshooting guidance for nesting batch jobs and workflows in XD.

Expand unit, integration, persistence, recovery, runtime-provider, Receptor, Spark, and parameterization tests; execute regression testing across affected modules; and diagnose and fix defects found during validation.

Update dependencies and build metadata, verify generated artifacts, perform code cleanup and API review, check documentation examples, prepare migration notes, and produce the final increment for delivery.
